speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the cesarean section and maternal diabetes raise concerns for potential meconium aspiration or neonatal respiratory distress syndrome. What is the baby's current respiratory rate, and are you noticing any grunting, nasal flaring, or retractions? Additionally, please provide the Apgar scores and the results of your initial screening. text: RESULTS: Respiratory_Rate: Elevated; Oxygen_Saturation: 88% on room air, improving with oxygen; Arterial_Blood_Gas: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, PaO2 60 mm Hg, HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5; Blood_Glucose: Normal for age. speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). While urinary tract infection can cause poor feeding and apnea, the presence of severe respiratory signs like cyanosis, nasal flaring, and retractions in a 32-week premature infant is most characteristic of surfactant deficiency. I am requesting a Chest_X-Ray to confirm the classic ground-glass appearance of RDS.
